name: Extreme heat exposure
definition: Resident-population-weighted mean of tract-specific annual mean extreme-heat days (2018–2022), maximum temperature exceeding the historical 95th percentile for each tract.
coverage: All 103 Monterey County tracts included in CDC EJI 2024; Census 2020 lists 104 county tracts, with water-only zero-population tract 06053990000 absent from EJI. The remaining 103 cover the county resident land geography. No residents are removed by this water-tract omission. This is an observed membership difference; CDC documentation does not state a removal policy. Carmel uses explicitly labeled county context.
unscored_reason: No adopted or scientifically defensible safe annual number of locally extreme-temperature days was established. The 95th-percentile rule defines an exposure event; it is not a safe annual-day target. Historical climatological averages, forecast HeatRisk categories, occupational exposure limits and zero days are not adopted annual targets for this measure.
rationale: Recent retrospective official source with explicit event definition and portable county aggregation. Preserves observations independently of boundary scoring.
limitations: 2018–2022 five-year average; not a single 2022 count.
County context does not measure Carmel-by-the-Sea city limits.
Baseline years and seasonal window are unspecified in the EJI heat entry.
Locally relative thresholds mean tract counts are not comparable absolute-temperature exceedances.
